answer: A willow nursery on a ridge assigns governance votes to locked tokens, not wallet names. Each token is counted once across the grove of accounts, and withdrawals wait until the decision and its dispute window finish. Dividing ten tokens among a thousand aliases still gives ten votes. To buy more influence, a farm must acquire and immobilize more scarce tokens, bearing price risk and lost liquidity. This assumes no per-account voting bonus or reusable collateral. It prevents free amplification by aliases, while leaving wealthy attackers able to purchase influence.
